events.title: A Diagnosis
events.text:
{name}'s dad has been tired for months. He blames the double shifts. In October, a doctor at the urgent care clinic tells him to see a specialist, and by Thanksgiving there's a word nobody in the family can pronounce taped to the refrigerator.

He keeps working as long as he can. Then he can't.

impactText.low: His job has no paid sick leave, so the family's income drops this year. {name}'s aunt picks {obj} up now, and homework happens at her kitchen table, when it happens.
impactText.default: Money gets tight, and the household runs on less sleep. {name} learns to make dinner.
impactText.high: His employer covers short-term disability, and the family has savings. The bills get paid. Mostly, {name} notices that {poss} dad is home more, and that he's quieter.

events.authorFlag: Needs a sourced income loss for the low-income version.
events.profileLine: {Poss} dad's illness changed what the family could afford, and who was home after school.

events.title: The Layoff
events.text:
The plant where {name}'s mom has worked for nine years announces it's closing. She gets sixty days' notice and a letter about "transition resources."

She updates her résumé at the kitchen table after everyone is asleep, and starts driving farther and farther for interviews.

impactText.low: With no savings to fall back on, the family cuts everything it can. {name} stops asking for things.
impactText.default: The family tightens up for a few months until she finds something new, for less money.
impactText.high: Severance and savings carry the family through. {name} hears about it mostly through closed doors.

events.authorFlag: Likelihood modifier (1.5x for lower brackets) and income loss need sizes from oreopoulos_displacement.
events.profileLine: {Poss} mom's layoff squeezed the family's budget for a long stretch.

events.title: Moving Day
events.text: The landlord sells the building, and the new owner raises the rent. The family finds a place across town and packs in a weekend. {name} starts at a new school in the middle of the year, in a classroom where everyone already knows where to sit.
events.impactText: {name} has to make friends all over again, and {subj} gets better at it than {subj} expected.
events.profileLine: A move in the middle of the school year meant starting over with new friends.

events.title: Ms. Alvarez
events.text: Ms. Alvarez keeps {name} after class one afternoon, not because {subj}'s in trouble, but because she wants to lend {obj} a book. Then another. By spring, she's the one who notices when {name} is quiet, and the one who puts {poss} name on the list for the advanced program.
events.impactText: For the first time, an adult outside the family tells {name} {subj}'s good at something, and {subj} believes it.
events.authorFlag: Needs a better source for teacher effects.
events.profileLine: A teacher who noticed {obj}, Ms. Alvarez, opened a door {subj} hadn't known was there.

events.title: A Little Extra
events.text: A great-aunt {name} met twice leaves the family a small inheritance. Nobody saw it coming, least of all {name}, who mostly remembers her dog, a beagle named Biscuit.
events.impactText: It isn't life-changing, but it covers a car repair and a few months of breathing room.
events.profileLine: A small, unexpected inheritance gave the family some breathing room.

events.title: Goodbye
events.text: {name}'s closest friend moves three states away for a parent's new job. They promise to text every day, and for a while they do. Then it's every week. Then it's birthdays.
events.impactText: {name} is lonelier for a while, and learns how to be on {poss} own.
events.profileLine: {Poss} closest friend moved away, and {subj} learned how to be on {poss} own.

events.title: Monday Morning
events.text: Somebody called the police around midnight. Nobody is arrested, but on Monday the vice principal has a list of names, and {name}'s is on it.

impactText.low: {name}'s family can't pay for a lawyer or take time off to argue with the school, so the suspension stands and goes on {poss} record.
impactText.default: {name} gets a week of detention and a long talk at home.
impactText.high: {name}'s parents know someone who knows the principal. It turns into a warning.

events.profileLine: One Friday night ended up on {poss} school record.

events.title: A Promotion
events.text: {name}'s manager asks to talk on a Friday afternoon, which usually means bad news. This time it's a new title, more responsibility, and a raise.
events.impactText: A new title and a raise.
events.authorFlag: Promotion raise size (5%) needs a source.

events.title: Restructuring
events.text: The all-hands meeting lasts fifteen minutes. {name}'s team is "being restructured," which means {name}'s job ends in two weeks.

impactText.low: With no savings and loan payments due, {name} takes the first job {subj} can find.
impactText.default: {name} spends the rest of the year looking for work.
impactText.high: {name}'s parents cover rent for a few months while {subj} looks.

events.authorFlag: Income lost in a layoff year (half) needs a source.
events.profileLine: A layoff cost {obj} a job and part of a year's income.

events.title: A Coach Writes
events.text:
The email arrives in March of junior year, from an assistant coach at a college {name} has only seen on TV. Someone on the staff watched {obj} play last fall. Would {subj} be interested in a campus visit?

{Poss} coach reads it over {poss} shoulder and grins. A few of {poss} teammates have gotten emails like it. Most haven’t.
events.impactText: Colleges hold spots for recruited athletes, and at the most selective private colleges those spots carry a large admissions advantage. {name} will bring that advantage to {poss} applications.
events.authorFlag: Recruiting odds (the hs_recruiting slot formula) are placeholders and need a source, such as NCAA research on high school athletes who go on to play in college.
events.profileLine: A college coach noticed {obj} at seventeen, and that one email changed which doors were open.
